articleTitle: Hysteresis control of a continuous boost regulator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: To comply with forthcoming mains harmonic distortion regulations, electronic equipment will require pre-regulators. For high voltage applications, where the DC output exceeds the peak mains supply voltage, the preferred option is a boost converter. The merits of continuous and discontinuous operation are discussed with reference to optimum solutions. The conventional control technique, average current mode control, shows instabilities under certain conditions. An alternative control technique, hysteresis control, is proposed and analysed. This technique is believed to exhibit greater stability. Four hysteresis control algorithms are presented. Practical implementations of these techniques are shown, together with a comparison of the measured circuit performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power factor correction using quasi-resonant SEPIC converter with three-phase input
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: A new combination of a 'unity power factor three-phase rectifier stage' with a quasi-resonant SEPIC converter, provides high quality input currents of a transformer isolated three-phase AC-DC converter. Analysis of the converter, including analysis of the three-phase input current waveforms, has been performed and a design procedure developed. Results of a transformer isolated 1.0 kW/35 kHz prototype converter, utilising a single 1200 V IGBT as the active switching device and operating direct off-line from a 415 V three-phase mains supply, are presented to verify theoretical predictions. The measured input current waveforms, drawn from the three-phase supply, approach unity power factor with little harmonic content.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the utilisation of the transformer parasitic capacitances as a resonant component in high voltage converters operating above resonance with variable frequency
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: The authors present a variable frequency resonant converter with an output inductor filter operating above resonance where the resonant circuit is constituted only of the transformer leakage inductance and the secondary parasitic capacitance referred to the primary side. First, they present the HV transformer equivalent circuit which is simplified and integrated in a series-parallel resonant converter. In the second place, the limits imposed by the behaviour of the transformer at high frequencies are discussed and included in the converter operation characteristics. Experimental validations are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A unity power factor sinusoidal supply side convertor for industrial AC drives
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: The authors present an overview of the techniques of sinusoidal rectification applied to the input of a variable speed voltage source inverter. The need for sinusoidal, unity power factor loads is an important consideration as more nonlinear loads are applied to the supply network. The incorporation of a line regeneration capability is also a major feature as users consider the energy efficiency of variable speed AC drive installations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The phase-shift controlled H-bridge DC-DC converter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: The kW range of DC-DC converters have shown the zero voltage switching phase-shift controlled H-bridge converter to have advantages over alternative circuits. Operation of the converter is described in detail for various load and circuit conditions, and illustrated with computer simulation results. A design procedure and discussion of tradeoffs follows. A new, improved, control technique is described which uses a modified switching pattern to improve the ZVS capability and to allow the maximum possible duty cycle.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast dynamic response rectifier with low input distortion
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: The authors describe a step-down rectifier for the provision of a stable and well regulated DC bus to supply the high-power, low-distortion amplifiers used in vibration test equipment. The voltage required is below the peak of the line-voltage of the three-phase supply. Low EMI from the rectifier is essential because of the sensitive measurement and control equipment used during vibration testing. The authors discuss both open loop and closed loop operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Matrix/sub x/ simulation of switched mode power converter systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: When using computer simulation techniques to assess and design control networks for power electronic systems it is often necessary to simulate the operation of the converter and its control circuit over many switching cycles. Matrix/sub x/ is a general purpose system simulation package in which systems are defined in terms of equations and block diagrams. A power converter may be represented in Matrix/sub x/ as a switched sequence of linear, time-invariant, state-space equations. Matrix/sub x/ simulation has been used to compare two alternative current control strategies for the phase-shift controlled converter. Average current mode control has been shown to offer improved performance both in terms of ensuring symmetrical transformer magnetisation and in producing a first-order dominated control-to-output characteristic. Close agreement with practical measurements has been demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A reversible 560 kVA converter using GTOs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Static Power Conversion
abstract: A reversible high power converter has been built and tested, to replace a motor generator set in a critical application. The converter has several novel features, particularly unconstrained parallel operation on the AC output, a high power and overload rating from a low voltage battery backed DC rail, high efficiency and low harmonic and RFI emission. The power and control circuit and measures to meet stringent performance, reliability, and environmental targets are described. Test results from operation in a 'small' power system, particularly with direct-on-line starting of large induction motors and instantaneous full load take up are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
